hoisin.name: Hoisin sauce
hoisin.watch: Check the label for oyster or shrimp extract. Most hoisin has none.

tamari.name: Tamari
tamari.watch: Check the label: most tamari is gluten-free, but not every brand.

tortilla-flour.name: Flour tortillas (8-inch)
tortilla-flour.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

tortilla-corn.name: Corn tortillas (6-inch)
tortilla-corn.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands don't use it.

sour-cream.name: Sour cream
sour-cream.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

cottage-cheese.name: Small-curd cottage cheese
cottage-cheese.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

beef-sirloin.name: Beef sirloin steak, about 1 inch thick

yogurt-greek.name: Plain Greek yogurt
yogurt-greek.watch: Check the label for gelatin. Pick a brand made without it.

refried-beans.name: Vegetarian refried beans
refried-beans.watch: Many refried beans are made with lard. Buy a can marked vegetarian, and check the label.

turkey-sausage-bulk.name: Bulk turkey breakfast sausage (no casing)
turkey-sausage-bulk.watch: Buy bulk turkey sausage, sold loose with no casing. Links often use pork casings, even when the meat is turkey.

tortilla-burrito.name: Burrito-size flour tortillas (10-inch)
tortilla-burrito.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

tortilla-gluten-free.name: Gluten-free tortillas
tortilla-gluten-free.watch: Check the label for lard. Most store brands use oil or vegetable shortening instead.

turkey-strips.name: Turkey bacon
turkey-strips.watch: Pick a package that says fully cooked.

chicken-sausage-smoked.name: Smoked chicken andouille sausage (fully cooked)
chicken-sausage-smoked.watch: Buy chicken andouille that's collagen-cased or skinless. Many chicken sausages are stuffed into pork casings, and some mix in pork, so read the whole label. Beef kielbasa works too, with the same checks.

beef-kielbasa.name: Beef kielbasa (fully cooked)
beef-kielbasa.watch: Buy kielbasa labeled all beef, collagen-cased or skinless. Most kielbasa is pork, and many beef ones still use pork casings, so read the whole label.

pot-large.name: Large heavy pot with a lid (like a Dutch oven)

shallow-dish.name: Wide shallow dish, like a pie plate

heatproof-bowl.name: Heatproof glass or metal bowl that sits on top of the saucepan

building-a-sauce.name: Building a sauce
building-a-sauce.idea: Layer flavor in one pan: fat, aromatics, spices, liquid, then simmer it down.

poaching-eggs.name: Gentle eggs
poaching-eggs.idea: Low, steady heat sets eggs all the way through without turning them rubbery.

thin-slicing.name: Thin slicing
thin-slicing.idea: Thin slices across the grain cook fast and stay tender.

marinating.name: Marinating
marinating.idea: A salty, sweet, or tangy soak flavors meat before it ever hits the pan.

cutting-in-fat.name: Cutting in cold fat
cutting-in-fat.idea: Little pieces of cold butter turn to steam in the oven and puff dough into flaky layers.

folding-layers.name: Folding for layers
folding-layers.idea: Folding dough over itself stacks the butter into thin layers.

browning-butter.name: Browning butter
browning-butter.idea: Cooking butter past melted toasts its milk solids and makes it taste nutty.

creaming.name: Creaming
creaming.idea: Beating soft butter with sugar traps air, and that air makes baked things softer and lighter.

julienne.name: Julienne
julienne.idea: Cut food into thin matchsticks so it cooks fast and rolls up neatly.

fine-chopping.name: Fine chopping
fine-chopping.idea: Chop herbs and vegetables into small, even bits so every bite gets some.

dicing.name: Dicing
dicing.idea: Cut into small cubes, all about the same size, so they cook evenly.

rolling-wrapping.name: Rolling and wrapping
rolling-wrapping.idea: Fill a wrapper snugly and roll it tight so it holds together.

dressings.name: Whisked dressings
dressings.idea: Whisking oil into something tangy makes a dressing that clings to food.

quick-pickling.name: Quick pickling
quick-pickling.idea: A hot vinegar brine turns crisp vegetables tangy in under an hour.

searing.name: High-heat searing
searing.idea: A very hot pan browns the outside fast, and browning is flavor.

broiling.name: Broiling
broiling.idea: Strong heat from above cooks thin food fast and chars the top.

heat-control.name: Heat control
heat-control.idea: Turning the heat up or down at the right time is most of cooking.

stir-frying.name: Stir-frying
stir-frying.idea: Small pieces, a very hot pan, and constant moving cook food in minutes.

simmering.name: Simmering
simmering.idea: Small, lazy bubbles cook gently without toughening food.

braising.name: Braising
braising.idea: Brown first, then cook slowly in a little liquid until tender.

reducing.name: Reducing
reducing.idea: Boiling off water makes a sauce thicker and its flavor stronger.

emulsions.name: Emulsions
emulsions.idea: Fat and water mix into a smooth sauce when you add them slowly and keep stirring.

crisping.name: Crisping
crisping.idea: Dry food and hot fat make a crunchy, golden crust.

timing.name: Timing a meal
timing.idea: Start the slowest part first so everything is ready together.

roux.name: Roux
roux.idea: Flour cooked in butter thickens milk or broth into a smooth sauce.

blooming-spices.name: Blooming spices
blooming-spices.idea: Spices wake up in hot fat, so a minute in the oil makes them taste stronger.

flavor-base.name: Flavor base
flavor-base.idea: Onions and their friends cooked slowly build the flavor everything else sits on.

spice-rubs.name: Spice rubs
spice-rubs.idea: A dry mix of spices rubbed on before cooking seasons the outside.

one-pot-stews.name: One-pot stews
one-pot-stews.idea: Build a whole meal in one pot, adding each part when it needs the time.

layering.name: Building in layers
layering.idea: Make each part well on its own, then stack them so every bite has all of them.

breaking-down-chicken.name: Breaking down a chicken
breaking-down-chicken.idea: Cutting a whole bird into pieces saves money and gives bones for stock.

making-stock.name: Making stock
making-stock.idea: Bones and vegetables simmered for hours make a broth with real flavor.

shredding.name: Shredding
shredding.idea: Meat braised until tender pulls apart into strands that soak up sauce.

masa-dough.name: Masa dough
masa-dough.idea: Corn masa mixed with water makes a dough you press and griddle.

pleating.name: Pleating and sealing
pleating.idea: Small folds seal a filling inside a wrapper so it stays put while cooking.

flatbreads.name: Flatbreads
flatbreads.idea: A soft dough rolled thin cooks in minutes in a very hot pan.

scalded-dough.name: Cooked doughs
scalded-dough.idea: Stirring flour or starch into hot liquid makes a dough that puffs and stays chewy.

muffin-method.name: The muffin method
muffin-method.idea: Mix wet and dry separately, then stir together only until just combined.

skillet-baking.name: Skillet baking
skillet-baking.idea: A preheated cast-iron pan gives batter a crisp, golden bottom.

yeast-dough.name: Yeast dough
yeast-dough.idea: Kneading builds stretch, and yeast fills the dough with air as it rises.

batters.name: Batters
batters.idea: A thin batter poured hot sets into crêpes, cakes, or a crisp coating.

filling-crimping.name: Filling and crimping
filling-crimping.idea: Fold dough over a filling and press the edge so nothing leaks.

stiff-porridge.name: Cornmeal porridge
stiff-porridge.idea: Stirring cornmeal into boiling water until it pulls from the pan makes a dough you eat by hand.

pastry.name: Pastry
pastry.idea: Cold butter, cold water, and a light touch make a crust that is crisp and tender.

layered-pastry.name: Phyllo
layered-pastry.idea: Paper-thin sheets brushed with fat bake into crackly layers.

custards.name: Custards
custards.idea: Eggs and milk baked gently set smooth instead of curdling.

breading-frying.name: Breading and shallow frying
breading-frying.idea: Flour, egg, crumbs, then hot oil a finger deep makes a crunchy crust.

deep-frying.name: Deep frying
deep-frying.idea: Food fried in oil at the right temperature cooks through and stays crisp, not greasy.

oven-browning.name: Oven browning
oven-browning.idea: Dry heat in the oven browns and crisps, with a stir partway for even color.

binders.name: Binders
binders.idea: Egg and crumbs hold ground meat together so it slices instead of crumbling.

roasting.name: Roasting and carving
roasting.idea: Roast, rest so the juices settle, then carve across the grain.

gravy.name: Pan gravy
gravy.idea: The browned bits in a roasting pan become gravy with a little flour and broth.

cooking-legumes.name: Cooking dried beans and lentils
cooking-legumes.idea: Dried beans and lentils simmer gently until they're soft all the way through; lentils need no soaking, beans cook faster after one.

temping-meat.name: Checking meat with a thermometer
temping-meat.idea: The only way to know ground meat is safe is to check the middle: 160°F for beef, 165°F for poultry.

sauteing.name: Sautéing
sauteing.idea: A hot pan and shimmering oil cook small pieces fast, so they brown outside before they go soft.

cooking-grains.name: Cooking grains
cooking-grains.idea: Grains drink a set amount of liquid; toast them first and leave the lid on, and every grain stays separate.

handling-poultry.name: Handling raw poultry
handling-poultry.idea: Raw chicken goes on its own board, never gets rinsed, and is followed by washing hands and everything it touched.

cooking-fish.name: Cooking fish
cooking-fish.idea: Fish is delicate and cooks fast; it's done when it turns opaque and flakes, at 145°F.

building-soup.name: Building a soup
building-soup.idea: A soup is built in layers: a base, a good stock, and seasoning tasted at every stage.

blanching.name: Blanching
blanching.idea: A quick dip in boiling water, then straight into ice water, keeps a vegetable bright and crisp and stops it cooking.

cooling-reheating.name: Cooling and reheating
cooling-reheating.idea: Cooked food cools fast in shallow containers, goes in the fridge within 2 hours, and is reheated to 165°F.

terms.means: Cut into small cubes about the size of a pea. Try to make them all close to the same size so they cook evenly.
Chop into tiny bits, smaller than a grain of rice. Keep rocking the knife back and forth over the pile until nothing big is left.
Cut into rough, bite-size pieces. They don't have to match.
Cut into flat pieces, like slices of bread.
Cut into thin sticks, about the size of a matchstick.
Rub food down a grater so it falls off in shreds. The big holes make shreds. The small holes make a paste.
Grate just the colored outside of a lemon or orange peel. Stop when you see white; the white part tastes bitter.
Cook a liquid with small, lazy bubbles that pop now and then. If big bubbles roll all over, turn the heat down.
Big bubbles rolling all over the pot, even while you stir.
Cook gently in liquid that's barely bubbling.
Cook in a little hot oil or butter, stirring often.
Cook in a very hot pan without moving the food, so the outside turns deep brown.
Brown the food first, then cook it slowly with a little liquid and the lid on until it's very tender.
Soak food in a flavorful liquid, called a marinade, before you cook it.
Stir fast in little circles with a whisk or a fork, to mix things together and add air.
Beat soft butter and sugar together hard until the mixture is fluffy and a little paler.
Lay the dough over itself in layers, like folding a letter to fit in an envelope.
Push the dough away with the heel of your hand, fold it back, turn it, and repeat until it's smooth and stretchy.
Sprinkle a thin, light layer, like flour on the counter so dough doesn't stick.
Gently lift and turn the food so every piece gets coated, like tossing a salad.
Hot oil looks wavy and rippled on top. That means it's hot enough for the food.
Meat has thin lines running through it, like the lines in wood. Cut across those lines, not along them, so each bite is tender.
Butter and flour cooked together, stirring, for a few minutes. It thickens milk or broth into a smooth sauce. Say it "roo."
Cook something for just a minute or two in boiling water, then scoop it straight into a bowl of ice water. The ice water stops the cooking, so it stays bright green and a little crunchy.
Pour a little liquid into a hot pan after browning, and scrape up the brown bits stuck to the bottom. They melt into the liquid and give the dish its deep, savory flavor.

units.4: Breaking down and slicing meat, marinades

lessons.label: 4a

lessons.label: 6b

lessons.label: 6c
lessons.title: Challah French toast

lessons.title: Crispy hash browns

lessons.label: 8a
lessons.title: Shakshuka
lessons.skill: Building a sauce, then poaching eggs in it
lessons.about: Eggs gently cooked in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, served in the pan with bread for dipping.

lessons.label: 8b
lessons.title: Spaghetti marinara
lessons.about: Spaghetti in a simple homemade tomato sauce with garlic and basil.

lessons.label: 8c
lessons.title: Honey-garlic chicken
lessons.about: Bite-size chicken in a sticky, sweet-savory honey, garlic, and soy sauce, over rice.

lessons.label: 9a
lessons.title: Chicken fried rice

lessons.label: 9b
lessons.title: Turkey lettuce wraps

lessons.title: Oyakodon
